No-show fee

He parked a bit away and cancelled on me.

Filed by
Rider

This is a provisional ruling made by an automated system.

Ruling

Fee stands, driver compensated DRIVER_COMPENSATION

The fee stands. The driver is paid SGD 3.60. No refund.

The judge's explanation, as written

The dispute is over the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02719 — the only amount contested, and the fare breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The driver ended the trip at 07:45:40 with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, and the fee stands. FOR THE DRIVER. Every condition of the baseline no-show clause (POL-NS-01) holds. (a) The trip record carries the 'I'm Here' arrival event at 07:39:37. (b) The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02719) places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from that same moment — the longest qualifying in-geofence run starts exactly at 07:39:37 (dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0) and contains 37 qualifying fixes. (c) That hold is continuous for 360 seconds against the 180-second free waiting period in force (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec), a surplus of 180 seconds; no_show_threshold_sec is null, so no longer threshold applies. (d) No boarding is recorded, and the cancellation at 07:45:40 falls after the required dwell elapsed (07:42:37), under RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes the clause recognises. Nothing displaces the fee: POL-NS-05 does not bite (the marker coincides with the first qualifying fix, and the closest approach is 41.42 m, far inside the 300 m trigger); POL-NS-06 does not bite (the dwell exceeds the minimum rather than falling short); POL-NS-03 does not apply (the driver was inside the radius, not outside it); POL-NS-10 does not apply (the driver, not the rider, cancelled). Compensation therefore follows at 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 fee in force: SGD 3.60, the same figure the payments ledger computes under POL-NS-07. The anti-farming check does not trip — driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the 4-or-more limb, and 1 divided by 133 completed trips in 30 days is 0.0075, below the 0.08 limb — so compensation is paid, not withheld. FOR THE RIDER. Your account that the driver 'parked a bit away' is borne out by the driver's own trace: his closest approach to the pickup pin across the whole trip was 41.42 m (driver_track.min_distance_m), while your device sat 2.73 to 10.55 m from that pin on 66 of 66 fixes. But 41.42 m is still inside the 50 m arrival radius POL-NS-02 sets for a STANDARD pickup, so it does not make the fee unchargeable — the driver had arrived within the policy's meaning, and his statement that he was 'right at the pin' is loose rather than decisive. Your strongest route, the rider-contact clause (POL-NS-04), fails at its first condition: it requires at least one message from you during the waiting window whose content locates or coordinates (your own position, an entrance, block, tower or bay identifier, a request for the driver's position, or a statement that you cannot see the vehicle), and your only message was 'ok' at 07:41:07, sent in reply to the driver's 'here'. 'ok' names no place, asks for nothing and tells the driver nothing about where you were — it is an acknowledgement, not locating or coordinating content, and the clause's enumerated content test is not met by it. The clause's other two conditions do hold — the driver neither replied within 120 seconds nor placed any in-app call before cancelling, and your track sits inside the 100 m presence radius on every fix — but POL-NS-04 requires all three, so it cannot exonerate you and the fee is not refunded. The wrong-entrance route (POL-NS-03) is closed because the driver was inside the arrival radius rather than outside it, and its pin-ambiguity goodwill branch is closed because trip_record.registered_pickup_points is 1, not the 2 or more that branch requires. ON EVIDENCE. EV-ADVIS-02719-01 (traffic advisory, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) has no payload and carries no fact; it is not relied on and changes nothing. The GPS trace, trip record, chat log, fare ledger and both profiles are each COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, with 100 percent GPS coverage, a 10-second cadence and a 0-second maximum gap inside the waiting window, and the fare line reconciles to the SGD 4.50 charged. The confidence cap is therefore 1.0, and no POL-NS-08 impairment or POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is present. OUTCOME. The contested SGD 4.50 fee is not refunded to the rider — it stands as charged. The driver is paid SGD 3.60, and the same figure appears in amount_sgd, which on a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling is the amount the ruling moves rather than a second payment. The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

How to appeal: Either party may appeal once within 30 days. A different human reviewer hears it, and only record evidence may be added.

Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

What each side argued

The rider advocate

kept The rider was at the pickup point for the whole waiting window. The rider's track in EV-GPS-02719 carries 66 fixing points, every one stationary (its only distinct speed is 0.0 km/h), with a maximum distance of 10.55 m and a mean of 6.73 m from the pickup pin, running from 07:37:49 to 07:47:33 - before the driver's 07:39:37 arrival marker and 113 seconds past the 07:45:40 cancellation. POL-NS-04 limb (c) is therefore satisfied, and satisfied strongly: the rider's device sat inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, and in fact within about 11 m of the pin, for all 66 qualifying fixes rather than merely the majority. That rider track is present, populated and unambiguous, so nothing about rider position is undecidable on this record.

evidence EV-GPS-02719, EV-TRIP-02719 · clauses POL-NS-04

kept The rider's message went unanswered by the driver. The chat log holds exactly two messages - the driver's 'here' at 07:39:57 and the rider's reply at 07:41:07 - and the driver neither posted another message nor placed an in-app voice call before terminating the trip at 07:45:40; trip_record.in_app_calls is empty. That is 273 seconds of driver silence after the rider's message, far outside the 120 second window, so POL-NS-04 limb (b) is satisfied.

evidence EV-CHAT-02719, EV-TRIP-02719 · clauses POL-NS-04

kept POL-NS-04 limb (a) is met on this record. The rider did send a message inside the waiting window - 'ok' at 07:41:07, delivered at 07:41:08 and read by the driver at 07:41:17 - in direct response to the driver's 'here'. The limb's list (the rider's own position, an entrance, block, tower or bay identifier, a request for the driver's position, or a statement that the vehicle cannot be seen) illustrates locating or coordinating content rather than closing it, and a reply that takes up the driver's position notice while the rider stands at the pin is coordination in substance: the driver's 'here' named no sub-location, entrance or bay that the rider could answer or move to, and the rider's message is the coordination the record contains.

evidence EV-CHAT-02719 · clauses POL-NS-04

kept The driver's own trace does not support his account that he was 'right at the pin'. The closest his vehicle ever came to the pickup pin across the entire trip was 41.42 m (driver_track.min_distance_m over 67 fixes), against a STANDARD arrival radius of 50 m under POL-NS-02 - a margin of 8.6 m, narrower than the 25 m accuracy filter the same clause applies to each fix - while the rider's device sat 2.73 to 10.55 m from that same pin. The rider's account that the driver 'parked a bit away' is corroborated by the driver's own measurement, and the counterparty statement is not.

evidence EV-GPS-02719, EV-TRIP-02719 · clauses POL-NS-02

kept The premise of the termination is not made out. The rider does not dispute the 360-second in-geofence interval in the driver's trace (derived.arrival.longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec, 07:39:37 to 07:45:37); the rider's case is that the trip was not ended by a rider who failed to appear. POL-NS-01 limb (d) requires the trip to have been terminated on the rider's failure to appear - the reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW is the record of that failure, and the fee exists for nothing else - yet the only measurement of the rider's position on this record places the rider at the pin, stationary, on 66 of 66 fixes across the window and still there 113 seconds after the cancellation. On that evidence limb (d) is not established and the cancellation fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01.

evidence EV-GPS-02719, EV-TRIP-02719 · clauses POL-NS-01

kept The money. fare_breakdown records a cancellation fee of SGD 4.50 charged to the rider at 07:45:57, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 - the whole amount contested here is that single fee line. On POL-NS-04 the rider is exonerated and the fee is refunded in full with no driver compensation payable, and under POL-GEN-03 FULL_REFUND means the filing party - the rider, per dispute.filed_by - has the whole contested amount returned and the present charge does not stand.

evidence EV-FARE-02719, EV-GPS-02719, EV-CHAT-02719 · clauses POL-NS-04, POL-GEN-03

The driver advocate

kept Limbs (a) and (b) of the anchor clause are both made out on the platform's own record. The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 07:39:37, and the GPS trace's single qualifying in-geofence run begins at exactly that timestamp (dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0), so the arrival marker and the first qualifying fix coincide — this is not an early-tap case. Over that hold the trace records 37 qualifying fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and the closest approach anywhere in the trace is 41.4 m. The rider's 'parked a bit away' therefore describes a position that is still inside the radius, and the radius is the whole of the arrival test under POL-NS-02: a driver need not stand on the pin, only within 50 m of it for this STANDARD zone class.

evidence EV-GPS-02719, EV-TRIP-02719 · clauses POL-NS-01, POL-NS-02

kept Limb (c) is satisfied with room to spare. The driver held position inside the geofence continuously for 360 seconds, from 07:39:37 to 07:45:37, against a free waiting period of 180 seconds read from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec for this trip. The derived shortfall_sec is -180.0, that is, the hold is double the minimum in force; platform_policy.no_show_threshold_sec is null, so no longer threshold applies on top.

evidence EV-GPS-02719, EV-TRIP-02719 · clauses POL-NS-01

kept Limb (d) is satisfied. The record shows no boarding event, and the trip was terminated by the driver at 07:45:40 — 363 seconds after the run began at the first qualifying in-geofence fix, so after the required dwell had elapsed — with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes limb (d) recognises. Nor is this a driver who could not find his rider: the rider's own track holds 66 qualifying fixes, all at 0.0 km/h, between 2.7 m and 10.6 m of the pickup pin; the rider read the driver's 'here' message at 07:40:27 and replied 'ok' at 07:41:07; and the rider still did not board during the remaining minutes in which the driver held position.

evidence EV-TRIP-02719, EV-GPS-02719, EV-CHAT-02719 · clauses POL-NS-01

kept No rider-exonerating clause displaces the fee on the waiting clock. POL-NS-06 refunds only where the effective in-geofence dwell falls short of the free waiting period in force, and it does not fall short here: the derived shortfall_sec is -180.0 against a 180 second minimum. Limb (i)'s accumulation-across-intervals route is never reached, because the trace shows one continuous qualifying interval, and the driver does not rely on it.

evidence EV-GPS-02719, EV-TRIP-02719 · clauses POL-NS-06

kept The false-arrival clause does not bite. Neither trigger of POL-NS-05 is present: the driver's closest approach at any point in the trace is 41.4 m, far inside the 300 m distance trigger, and the arrival marker at 07:39:37 coincides with the first qualifying in-geofence fix — which is why the derived dwell_start_offset_sec is 0.0 and no recomputation of the waiting clock was required. The marker is effective and starts the clock as POL-NS-01(c) reads it.

evidence EV-TRIP-02719, EV-GPS-02719 · clauses POL-NS-05, POL-NS-01

kept POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider, because limb (a) fails at the first step. That limb requires a rider message whose content is locating or coordinating — the rider's own position, an entrance, block, tower or bay identifier, a request for the driver's position, or a statement that the rider cannot see the vehicle. The chat log holds exactly two messages: the driver's 'here' at 07:39:57, and the rider's 'ok' at 07:41:07 in reply. 'ok' names no position and no entrance or bay and asks for nothing; it is an acknowledgement that the driver had messaged, not coordination of a meet-up, and on that text the clause does not apply.

evidence EV-CHAT-02719, EV-TRIP-02719 · clauses POL-NS-04

kept The rider's own explanation is the wrong-entrance route of POL-NS-03, and that clause is not open on this record. POL-NS-03 applies only where the driver's stationary fixes lie OUTSIDE the POL-NS-02 arrival radius but within 400 m, whereas every fix in this hold lies inside the radius — 37 qualifying fixes within 50 m, closest approach 41.4 m. The pin-ambiguity branch is closed too: trip_record.registered_pickup_points is 1, not the 2 or more limb (ii) requires, so no goodwill payment arises and no part of the fee is refundable on a 'parked a bit away' theory.

evidence EV-GPS-02719, EV-TRIP-02719 · clauses POL-NS-03, POL-NS-02

kept Where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and nothing from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, POL-NS-07 fixes the payout at 80 percent of the fee in force for the trip: 80 percent of SGD 4.50 is SGD 3.60, which is the figure the payments ledger's own money block computes. The anti-farming check does not trip, so compensation is not withheld and the case does not escalate on that ground: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the 4-or-more limb, and 1 divided by 133 completed trips in 30 days is 0.0075, below the 0.08 limb. Compensation is therefore payable and the fee stands as charged.

evidence EV-FARE-02719, EV-DPROF-02719, EV-TRIP-02719 · clauses POL-NS-07, POL-NS-01

evidence EV-ADVIS-02719-01, EV-GPS-02719 · clauses POL-NS-06, POL-GEN-02

The dispute is over the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02719 — the only amount contested, and the fare breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The driver ended the trip at 07:45:40 with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, and the fee stands. FOR THE DRIVER. Every condition of the baseline no-show clause (POL-NS-01) holds. (a) The trip record carries the 'I'm Here' arrival event at 07:39:37. (b) The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02719) places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from that same moment — the longest qualifying in-geofence run starts exactly at 07:39:37 (dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0) and contains 37 qualifying fixes. (c) That hold is continuous for 360 seconds against the 180-second free waiting period in force (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec), a surplus of 180 seconds; no_show_threshold_sec is null, so no longer threshold applies. (d) No boarding is recorded, and the cancellation at 07:45:40 falls after the required dwell elapsed (07:42:37), under RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes the clause recognises. Nothing displaces the fee: POL-NS-05 does not bite (the marker coincides with the first qualifying fix, and the closest approach is 41.42 m, far inside the 300 m trigger); POL-NS-06 does not bite (the dwell exceeds the minimum rather than falling short); POL-NS-03 does not apply (the driver was inside the radius, not outside it); POL-NS-10 does not apply (the driver, not the rider, cancelled). Compensation therefore follows at 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 fee in force: SGD 3.60, the same figure the payments ledger computes under POL-NS-07. The anti-farming check does not trip — driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the 4-or-more limb, and 1 divided by 133 completed trips in 30 days is 0.0075, below the 0.08 limb — so compensation is paid, not withheld. FOR THE RIDER. Your account that the driver 'parked a bit away' is borne out by the driver's own trace: his closest approach to the pickup pin across the whole trip was 41.42 m (driver_track.min_distance_m), while your device sat 2.73 to 10.55 m from that pin on 66 of 66 fixes. But 41.42 m is still inside the 50 m arrival radius POL-NS-02 sets for a STANDARD pickup, so it does not make the fee unchargeable — the driver had arrived within the policy's meaning, and his statement that he was 'right at the pin' is loose rather than decisive. Your strongest route, the rider-contact clause (POL-NS-04), fails at its first condition: it requires at least one message from you during the waiting window whose content locates or coordinates (your own position, an entrance, block, tower or bay identifier, a request for the driver's position, or a statement that you cannot see the vehicle), and your only message was 'ok' at 07:41:07, sent in reply to the driver's 'here'. 'ok' names no place, asks for nothing and tells the driver nothing about where you were — it is an acknowledgement, not locating or coordinating content, and the clause's enumerated content test is not met by it. The clause's other two conditions do hold — the driver neither replied within 120 seconds nor placed any in-app call before cancelling, and your track sits inside the 100 m presence radius on every fix — but POL-NS-04 requires all three, so it cannot exonerate you and the fee is not refunded. The wrong-entrance route (POL-NS-03) is closed because the driver was inside the arrival radius rather than outside it, and its pin-ambiguity goodwill branch is closed because trip_record.registered_pickup_points is 1, not the 2 or more that branch requires. Decision addressed to both parties. The contested amount is the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee on EV-FARE-02719 (cancellation_fee 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). All four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold, so the charge stands. (a) EV-TRIP-02719 carries the driver's 'arrived' event at 07:39:37. (b) EV-GPS-02719 places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius of POL-NS-02: 37 fixes qualify under the 25 m accuracy filter, and the qualifying run begins at exactly 07:39:37 (dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0), so the marker and the first in-geofence fix coincide and no POL-NS-05 recomputation is required. (c) The driver held position inside the radius continuously for 360 s, 07:39:37 to 07:45:37, against this trip's 180 s free waiting period (EV-TRIP-02719 platform_policy.free_wait_sec); platform_policy.no_show_threshold_sec is null. (d) There is no boarding event and the driver terminated at 07:45:40 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, 183 s after the 180 s dwell elapsed at 07:42:37. No clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06, and none of POL-NS-10, displaces the fee. POL-NS-07 therefore fixes the payout at 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 net fee = SGD 3.60, which is the figure EV-FARE-02719's money block computes; the anti-farming check does not trip (driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d 1 is below 4, and 1/133 completed trips in 30 days = 0.0075 is below 0.08), so the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION and the SGD 3.60 is both the compensation and the amount this ruling moves. The fee itself is not refunded. Rider: I accept your two main facts. Your track in EV-GPS-02719 places you at the pin throughout - 66 fixes, all stationary (0.0 km/h), 2.7 m to 10.6 m from the pin, 07:37:49 to 07:47:33 - inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, and the driver's closest approach was 41.42 m, so your 'parked a bit away' is corroborated by his own trace and his 'I was right at the pin' is not. But neither fact decides the case: 41.42 m is still inside the 50 m radius POL-NS-02 defines as arrival, and the radius, not the pin, is the test; rider position is answered by POL-NS-04, not by the arrival clause. POL-NS-04 needs all three limbs and fails at limb (a): it requires a rider message whose content is locating or coordinating, and 'ok' at 07:41:07 names no position, entrance, block or bay, asks for nothing and does not say you could not see the vehicle. Limbs (b) and (c) are made out (driver silent for 273 s, no in-app call; you at the pin on every admissible fix), but limb (a) is not, so the clause does not exonerate you. I also reject your submission that POL-NS-01(d) fails because you were present: limb (d) is a test on the trip record - no boarding event, termination under one of the three recognised reason codes at or after the dwell - and this record satisfies it; the only in-radius outcome in which POL-NS-01 itself refunds is a cancellation recorded DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which is not the code here. POL-NS-03 is not open either: every stationary fix lies inside the arrival radius, and registered_pickup_points is 1, not the 2 or more limb (ii) requires, so no pin-ambiguity goodwill arises. Driver: your limbs (a) to (d) and your reading of POL-NS-05, POL-NS-06 and POL-NS-03 are accepted. One correction to your own account: your closest approach was 41.42 m, not the pin itself; the 50 m radius makes that immaterial, and the trace is dense (10 s cadence, 100.0 percent coverage, 0 s maximum gap), so the arrival test could be run properly. You were right not to assert POL-NS-06(i): EV-ADVIS-02719-01 is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0) and carries nothing, and the hold is a single continuous 360 s interval, so accumulation is unnecessary and the shortfall is -180 s. Evidence and confidence: the facts that decide this case are carried by EV-GPS-02719 and EV-TRIP-02719, both weight_multiplier 1.0 and COMPLETE, so under POL-GEN-02(2) my confidence is capped at 1.0; I set it at 0.9. The driver's statement carries no weight_multiplier, so it enters neither the minimum nor the maximum of that cap. No POL-NS-09 trigger is present: disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 on both sides, no_show_disputes_30d is 0, no admissible artifact contradicts another on arrival, dwell or rider presence, and no deciding artifact is impaired. Under POL-GEN-01 the only profile fields used are those POL-NS-07 names. The monetary effect is SGD 3.60, below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold of POL-GEN-05, so it is executed on issue.
